subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` validation at config write time warn only, fail closed for unknown names, or stay audit-only because custom/plugin command IDs may exist?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but changing config-write behavior on a security-sensitive allow/deny surface affects custom/plugin command IDs and operator workflows, so automation should not choose the policy unilaterally.

options.title: Warn on unknown names
options.body: Reuse the security audit command catalog and suggestions in `openclaw config set/patch` while still allowing custom/plugin commands to be saved.

options.title: Fail closed on unknown names
options.body: Reject unknown denylist entries during config writes and require an explicit custom-command escape hatch or allowlist story.

options.title: Keep audit-only
options.body: Leave config writes permissive and rely on `openclaw security audit` to diagnose ineffective denylist entries after the fact.

recommendation.title: Warn on unknown names
recommendation.body: Reuse the security audit command catalog and suggestions in `openclaw config set/patch` while still allowing custom/plugin commands to be saved.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work on node command policy makes this the strongest available routing signal, though the final security/product call may need a repository owner.
